classification.classification_note: The saved MSAN trace reports a use-of-uninitialized-value at the second delete because the freed nodestore entry is poisoned after deallocation; the underlying source bug is stale-pointer reuse after `addParentAndTypeRef` deletes the inserted node.

bug_description.original: Detailed report: OSS-Fuzz issue 6574 on open62541 (`libFuzzer_open62541_fuzz_binary_message`) reports `Use-of-uninitialized-value` with crash state `NodeId_deleteMembers -> UA_deleteMembers -> UA_Node_deleteMembers` under MemorySanitizer.
bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta sample_info.json issue description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json
bug_description.normalized: The staged 670-byte OPC UA binary witness reaches `processMSG`, whose decoded service id selects `Service_AddNodes`. `UA_decodeBinary` materializes an `UA_AddNodesRequest`, and `Service_AddNodes` / `UA_Server_processServiceOperations` pass one decoded `UA_AddNodesItem` from its `nodesToAdd` array into `Operation_addNode_begin`; the saved artifacts do not establish which array index was selected when the crash occurred. `Operation_addNode_begin` allocates a new node, inserts it into the nodestore, and then calls `addParentAndTypeRef` with the raw inserted `UA_Node *`. On the witnessed path, `checkParentReference` rejects that item's decoded parent/reference combination, and `addParentAndTypeRef` takes its early failure branch at line 707 and deletes the just-inserted node via `UA_Server_deleteNode(server, node->nodeId, true)`. `deleteNodeOperation` removes the nodestore entry and releases the last nodestore reference, so the node storage is freed. Control then returns to `Operation_addNode_begin`, which still holds the stale `node` pointer and runs its own error cleanup `UA_Nodestore_delete(server, node)`. That second delete walks the freed node structure and MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` when `NodeId_deleteMembers` switches on the freed `nodeId.identifierType`. The fix changes `addParentAndTypeRef` to take a node id, reacquire a nodestore reference, and delete by node id instead of reusing the stale raw pointer.

source.description: First project-side materialization of vulnerability-relevant attacker state: `processMSG` decodes the service NodeId from the attacker-controlled OPC UA `MSG` body into `requestTypeId`, creating the dispatch key that drives the message into AddNodes handling.
source.value_from: The staged witness is the saved 670-byte raw OPC UA conversation at `gt_results/arvo_6574/poc`, beginning with `HELF` and `OPNF` before the crashing `MSG`. The decoded `MSG` service id later hits `UA_NS0ID_ADDNODESREQUEST_ENCODING_DEFAULTBINARY` in `getServicePointers`, so this `UA_NodeId_decodeBinary` call is the first project statement that turns attacker bytes into the AddNodes dispatch key.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.code: retval = addParentAndTypeRef(server, session, node, parentNodeId, referenceTypeId, &item->typeDefinition.nodeId);
root_cause.description: Root cause. After `UA_Nodestore_insert` has transferred ownership of the new node into the nodestore, `Operation_addNode_begin` still passes the raw `UA_Node *node` and the callback-selected item's parent/reference/type data into `addParentAndTypeRef` without acquiring a nodestore reference. If that helper deletes the node on an error path, the caller's `node` alias becomes dangling but is still reused in the caller's own error cleanup.
root_cause.note: The fix commit changes this exact call to pass `&node->nodeId` and rewrites `addParentAndTypeRef` to reacquire the protected nodestore reference with `UA_Nodestore_get` before examining or deleting the node.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. During the second delete of the already freed nodestore entry, cleanup reaches `NodeId_deleteMembers` and branches on the freed `nodeId.identifierType` field.
sink.note: The crashing call chain in the saved trace is `UA_Nodestore_delete -> UA_NodeMap_deleteNode -> deleteEntry -> UA_Node_deleteMembers -> UA_deleteMembers -> deleteMembers_noInit -> NodeId_deleteMembers`.

parser_admitted.description: The decoded service id is admitted as `UA_NS0ID_ADDNODESREQUEST_ENCODING_DEFAULTBINARY` and dispatched to `Service_AddNodes`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The generic binary decoder zero-initializes the stack request object and materializes `nodesToAddSize` plus the decoded `nodesToAdd` array from attacker bytes. The later crashing callback consumes one `UA_AddNodesItem` from that array, but the saved artifacts do not establish a concrete index `i`.
tainted_value_origin.note: The saved free stack proves the decoded AddNodes request body reaches `UA_Server_processServiceOperations` and `Operation_addNode_begin`; the exact crashing array index and the exact failing `checkParentReference` sub-check are not recoverable from the staged artifacts.

fine_trace.note: Decodes the attacker-controlled service NodeId from the OPC UA `MSG` body. On the witnessed path this produces the numeric dispatch key later mapped to AddNodes handling.
Uses the decoded numeric NodeId from step 1 to select `Service_AddNodes` and `UA_TYPES[UA_TYPES_ADDNODESREQUEST]` for this message, admitting the input into the AddNodes parser/service path.

Zero-initializes and decodes the AddNodesRequest body selected in step 2, materializing `nodesToAddSize` and the `nodesToAdd` array. The later crashing callback consumes one decoded `UA_AddNodesItem` from this array, but the saved artifacts do not identify a concrete index.

Called from `Service_AddNodes` with `&request->nodesToAddSize`, this helper uses `ops = *requestOperations` from line 392 and reads the adjacent `request->nodesToAdd` pointer into `reqOp`, then invokes `Operation_addNode` on the current `UA_AddNodesItem` at `reqOp`. The staged trace proves one decoded array element reaches the callback, but not which loop iteration `i` crashes.

The callback-selected array element from step 4 becomes the typed `item` argument to `Operation_addNode_begin`; this call also aliases that same element's parent node id and reference type fields as separate arguments. `item` itself continues to carry the decoded `typeDefinition.nodeId` and `nodeClass` used later on the same path.
For the callback-selected `UA_AddNodesItem`, allocates a new heap-backed nodestore node of the item's decoded `nodeClass`.

Inserts the new node into the nodestore and copies its node id to `outNewNodeId`. In the default nodestore, `UA_NodeMap_insertNode` stores the entry in the hash slot at lines 360-366 without incrementing `refCount`, so the caller still keeps only an unprotected raw alias `node`.

fine_trace.code: retval = addParentAndTypeRef(server, session, node, parentNodeId, referenceTypeId, &item->typeDefinition.nodeId);
fine_trace.note: Root cause. After step 7 transfers ownership to the nodestore, `Operation_addNode_begin` still passes the raw `node` pointer plus the callback-selected item's decoded parent/reference/type fields into `addParentAndTypeRef`. Because no nodestore reference was acquired for that caller-held alias, any in-helper deletion turns `node` dangling.

The callback-selected AddNodes item fails `checkParentReference`, so `addParentAndTypeRef` takes this early error branch and deletes the just-inserted node by `node->nodeId` before returning. The saved free stack pins the invalidation to this exact line-707 branch, but it does not reveal which internal sub-check inside `checkParentReference` failed.

`UA_Server_deleteNode` first reacquires the nodestore entry by node id at line 1247, which increments its temporary refcount. `removeDeconstructedNode` marks the entry deleted, and `UA_Nodestore_release` at line 1267 decrements that temporary reference; `cleanupEntry` then frees the deleted entry when `refCount == 0`. MSAN's origin stack reports the poisoned bytes were created by this heap deallocation.

Control returns to `Operation_addNode_begin` with the same raw pointer from step 8. Because `retval` is non-GOOD, the caller runs its own error cleanup and passes stale pointer `node` into `UA_Nodestore_delete` a second time.

Sink. The second delete in step 11 reaches `UA_NodeMap_deleteNode -> deleteEntry -> UA_Node_deleteMembers -> UA_deleteMembers -> deleteMembers_noInit -> NodeId_deleteMembers`, and this `switch` reads and branches on freed `nodeId.identifierType` bytes from the node released in step 10. MemorySanitizer reports the resulting use-of-uninitialized-value here.

free_context.description: MSAN's origin stack says the later poisoned value was created by a heap deallocation when `deleteNodeOperation` released the just-deleted nodestore node.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch `b52793f9b872c1dc8452d504910ca6759bbef5c6` changes `addParentAndTypeRef` to take a node id, reacquire the nodestore reference with `UA_Nodestore_get`, release that reference at cleanup, and delete by node id rather than reusing the stale raw pointer. It also applies the same protection to the related `copyChildNode` call site.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The saved artifacts prove the invalidation happens on the early `checkParentReference` failure branch at `addParentAndTypeRef:707` and that the later poisoned read originates from the heap deallocation at `deleteNodeOperation:1267`. They do not reveal which `request->nodesToAdd[i]` element `UA_Server_processServiceOperations` passed to the crashing callback or which individual sub-check inside `checkParentReference` returned the error.

poc.trigger: Run `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_6574 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` with the staged `poc`; `reproduction_report.json` records `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `NodeId_deleteMembers`.

format.name: raw OPC UA HEL/OPN/MSG binary conversation
format.contract: The exact staged witness is the saved 670-byte raw binary conversation at `gt_results/arvo_6574/poc`, beginning with `HELF` and `OPNF` before the crashing `MSG`. On the observed path, the `MSG` body must decode to `requestTypeId = UA_NS0ID_ADDNODESREQUEST_ENCODING_DEFAULTBINARY` and then to a non-empty AddNodes request whose `nodesToAdd` array contains at least one `UA_AddNodesItem` that `UA_Server_processServiceOperations` passes to `Operation_addNode_begin`. For that callback-selected item, the decoded parent/reference/type data must make `checkParentReference` return an error inside `addParentAndTypeRef` after the new node has been inserted into the nodestore. That error path deletes the inserted node via `UA_Server_deleteNode(server, node->nodeId, true)`, after which `Operation_addNode_begin` still executes `UA_Nodestore_delete(server, node)` on the stale raw pointer. This contract is limited to the staged witness and the observed validation-failure branch; the saved artifacts do not establish which `nodesToAdd` index the crashing callback used or which internal `checkParentReference` sub-check failed.
